title: What the day looked like at the close
text: Today was a very rough day. The S&P 500 fund SPY fell 4.4% to $733.11, and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ fell 6.5%. All 17 names on the list went down. The steadiest were the dividend fund SCHD (down 2.2%), Alphabet (down 2.2%) and Amazon (down 2.2%). The hardest hit were AMD (down 17.3%), Vertiv (down 14.1%) and Rocket Lab (down 12.2%). Big one day drops like this are rare, but they do happen. Tomorrow, watch whether prices keep falling, steady out, or bounce. Nobody can know which one in advance.

title: Chip and equipment makers fell much more than the big AI companies
text: The four big AI companies (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta) fell about 3% on average today. The five companies that sell parts and equipment for AI (NVIDIA, Broadcom, TSMC, Vertiv, AMD) fell about 12% on average. Broadcom now sits just 0.5% above its 52 week low. The 52 week range is the lowest and highest price in the past year. News reports say worries about AI spending drove the sell-off, but the exact reasons are still being sorted out.

title: Analyst targets are far above today's prices
text: A price target is where an analyst guesses a stock could be in about a year. The average target for NVIDIA is $339.17, but it closed at $181.60. For AMD it is $645.82 against $404.40. Be careful: targets are updated slowly, so many were set before today's drop. A big gap can mean a bargain, or it can mean the targets are out of date. It is a clue, never a promise.

title: Interest rates are still the highest in a year
text: The average 10 year Treasury yield was 5.13% in October. A year earlier it was about 4.06%. The 10 year Treasury yield is what the US government pays to borrow money for 10 years. When it is high, safe bonds look more attractive, and fast growing tech stocks can look less attractive. Watch whether it keeps climbing.

title: Lesson 39: What is panic selling?
text: Panic selling is when people rush to sell because prices are falling and they are scared, not because they have a plan. Here is the problem. If you sell after a big drop, you turn a temporary paper loss into a real one. Also, nobody can predict the exact bottom. Look at history: stocks have fallen sharply many times, like in April 2025, and then later recovered, though that is never guaranteed. Before investing, ask yourself two things. How long can I leave this money alone? How would I feel if it fell 20% in a week? If the honest answer is 'I would hate it', that is useful to know, and a mix of steadier investments might fit better. Planning for bad days in advance is much easier than deciding during one.

title: What this update covers
text: Prices come from the market close on November 5. Analyst targets and ratios are available for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Lockheed Martin and GE only. Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical have price data but no analyst targets or ratios. The reasons for today's moves come from news reports and could not all be checked. This is information to learn from, not advice to buy or sell.
